title: Fjordway Utilities onramp field journal
content:
Quick capture from 2026-02-24 call with Fjordway Utilities (ops + infra + data science). Informal notes / working list — lots unresolved, want to lock next steps by Mar 3

Attendees:
- Tara Hjelm (Fjordway CTO)
- Jonas Pettersen (Infrastructure lead)
- Mei Chen (Data & Models)
- Maya Singh (Redwood SE)
- Diego Alvarez (Redwood Solutions Eng)

Meeting objective:
- Understand inference needs for outage-prediction assistant and customer chat assistant running on field tablets + internal ops dashboards. Clarify deployment mode (private vpc vs on-prem), SLOs, data residency + encryption, and initial pilot scope.

High-level constraints / context:
- Customer: mid-size municipal utility covering coastal region, strict EU data residency requirement for customer PII, but engineering team in Oslo/Stockholm.
- Primary endpoints: 1) field technician chat (tablet) for troubleshooting, 2) internal incident summarization from SCADA logs, 3) customer response assistant (canned answers, no PII in responses).
- Expected peak QPS: 40 requests/sec during incident spikes, baseline ~5 qps. Typical prompt length 200-600 tokens, responses 50-250 tokens.
- On-premises preferred for SCADA integration (air-gapped option for sensitive pipelines). VPC option acceptable for chat assistant.

Latency & availability targets (customer asks):
- 95th perc latency <= 450ms for chat assistant (token stream acceptable)
- Batch summarization jobs can be async, throughput-oriented (minutes ok)
- SLA: 99.9% for dedicated deployment after pilot

Security / compliance notes:
- Must integrate with their HSM (Azure Key Vault with HSM-backed keys) and internal KMS; Redwood Private must be configured with customer KMS.
- Audit logs retention 7 years for incident summaries (they asked us to confirm retention capabilities).
- Network: peering to Fjordway VNet, strict egress IP allowlist; mTLS to control plane.
- Data flow: telemetry + SCADA -> internal preprocessing -> inference. They will NOT send raw SCADA frames; preprocessing team will extract events. Need to document PII redaction step in ingestion.

Model / runtime considerations (initial recommendation):
- Use a 13B open model quantized (8-bit / 4-bit depending on hw) for decent accuracy vs cost on Dedicated pool. Suggest 13B for chat; fallback smaller model (7B) for contention.
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated context (work orders) to reduce per-token cost for field tablets.
- Streaming enabled for chat; function-calling disabled initially (they want deterministic plaintext answers).
- Suggested batch sizes: low-latency path: batch <= 2 across tablets; throughput path (summaries) use batching up to 16. Need to validate with their request distribution.

Operational gotchas called out by customer / our notes:
- Tablet networks are flaky (LTE, boatyards): need strong fallback & retry policy; prefer streaming + partial response over long blocking timeouts.
- They use a custom compression on telemetry; we need sample payloads to verify preprocessing integration (action: Jonas to share sample files).
- SCADA-derived prompts include numeric tables — tokenizer quirks can blow up tokens if we include raw CSV; canonicalization and trimming rules needed.
- Internal ops want transcript retention for 7 years -> cost/retention policy + redact PII at ingestion or use tokenization-based minimization.
- Firewall rules: they require no outbound to general internet from inference nodes in private deployment. Need to confirm whether Redwood control plane requires egress for heartbeats; propose proxying control-plane metrics through allowed channel.

Instrumentation / eval plan:
- Build an eval set of 150 field prompts (real anonymized) + 60 incident-summaries for regression checks. We will run automated quality checks: ROUGE/ROUGE-L + a small human checklist (accuracy of instructions, hallucination rate).
- Define latency test harness using k6 script with realistic token distributions (Diego to produce).
- QPS profiling: create per-route dashboards in Redwood Console; pre-configure traces for token-level timing and kernel selection heatmaps.

Action items / owners (short):
- Jonas: share SCADA sample payloads + network diagram by 2026-02-27.
- Tara: internal security checklist + legal contact for data residency by 2026-03-01.
- Maya: draft private deployment architecture + KMS integration notes (include mTLS pattern) — deliver by 2026-03-03.
- Diego: k6 latency scripts + initial batch config suggestions — deliver by 2026-03-03.
- Mei: anonymized eval set sampling criteria + 50 example prompts by 2026-03-05.

Pilot scope proposal (what we discussed):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): narrow POC with sample prompts on Redwood Hosted sandbox to validate prompt format and tokenization; no PII.
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): Private deployment (VPC-connected) for field chat assistant on 2 GPUs (dedicated pool), streaming enabled, KV caching. Collect metrics, run evals, tune batching/quantization.
- Phase 2 (8 weeks): On-prem packaged deployment optional for SCADA summarization pipeline; add long-term retention and HSM integration; can be parallel with Phase 1.

Open questions to resolve in next call:
- Exact VM/GPU types they can host for on-prem (NVIDIA A10/A30/A100?) — influences quantization strategy.
- Do they require model weights to be stored in their HSM vault or just keys for envelope encryption?
- Which logs are allowed to leave the VPC (we proposed only metrics + trace summaries, no prompt/response text).
- Legal: which specific fields in transcripts count as PII for them (phone numbers, account numbers, location coords?)

Prompt snippets (examples collected quickly):
- Technician chat: "Issue: transformer tripped after salt spray. Last 3 events: [event table]. Steps we tried: [x]. Recommend next troubleshooting steps and likely fault cause (brief)."
- Summarization: "SCADA incident feed: [preprocessed bullet events]. Produce a 3-sentence executive summary and a 5-step remediation checklist."

Notes to self / heuristics to try during tuning:
- Trim repeated sensor timestamps while preserving order to save tokens.
- Use structured output templates to limit hallucinations (e.g., JSON list of steps). Customer wanted natural text for technicians but structured for internal dashboards.
- Enable low-temperature + constrained decode for summarization to reduce hallucination risk.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Send this capture + proposed pilot plan to Tara & Jonas by EOD 2026-02-25.
- Set 30-min sync on Mar 3 to sign off pilot scope (Maya to set calendar invite).

Random scratch ideas captured in the call (unvetted):
- Local on-device small LLM as ultra-low-latency fallback for extreme connectivity drops (tiny distilled 1-2B).
- Push lightweight ingest redaction library to their preprocessing pipeline (open-source we maintain) so they can verify PII rules locally.

End note: keep these in drive as working doc. Will produce a cleaned SOW draft once we get the SCADA samples and legal checklist.

-- Maya
